territorial_scope.description: Applies to US federal agencies and recipients of federal grants, with funded processing and pilot projects located in the United States.

evidence.quote: the processing or recycling of critical minerals in the United States

summary.short: Selected sections of the US Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act: federal grants, pilots and reports on AI-relevant sectors (critical minerals, smart manufacturing, automated and connected transport), directed at federal agencies, research institutions, states and grantees. Binding statute; obligations run from enactment or stated deadlines.
summary.long: Selected sections (not the full Act) of the US Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. Sec. 40210 directs the Secretary, with the NSF Director, to make competitive basic-research awards on critical minerals mining and recycling, including AI for geological exploration, and creates a grant program for pilot processing projects capped at $10,000,000 per grant, barring export of processed minerals to foreign entities of concern. Sec. 40433 requires a one-year report on digital tools, including AI, as climate solutions. Secs. 40531-40535 define smart manufacturing (including AI), expand industrial assessment centers, study national-laboratory computing access for small and medium manufacturers, and authorize state grants up to $2,000,000 with a 30 percent match. Sec. 11401 amends 23 U.S.C. 151 to fund charging and fuelling infrastructure with an 80 percent federal share. Sec. 13005 sets a $5,000,000 annual pilot on automated-vehicle effects on pavement. Sec. 25005 funds SMART grants for smart-city and transport technologies, including automated vehicles, with shares by community size and a GAO review. Sec. 25017 amends 49 U.S.C. 5505 to add cybersecurity of connected and autonomous vehicles to university transportation centre research. Duties bind federal agencies and grant recipients; the excerpt contains no penalty provisions.

notes: Excerpt only: Secs. 40210, 40433, 40531-40535, 11401, 13005, 25005 and 25017 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. The rest of the Act is not in the document, so relations and entities cover these sections only. Bracketed AGORA headings are not statutory text and were disregarded. 'Secretary' (Secs. 40210, 40433, 40533, 40534) and 'Department' (Sec. 40531) are not defined in the excerpt, so the responsible agency is often not named. Sec. 40210(a)(5)(D)(iii) has an unbalanced closing parenthesis in the source. Target ids and identifiers are blank where not applicable or not in the registry.

obligations.summary: A SMART grant may not be used to reimburse preaward or application preparation costs, for traffic or parking enforcement, or to purchase or lease a license plate reader.

evidence.quote: A SMART grant shall not be used

obligations.summary: Each eligible entity receiving a SMART grant must submit an implementation report to the Secretary describing deployment and operational costs compared with benefits, and goal achievement; it is repeated annually until the grant is expended.
obligations.applies_from: Not later than 2 years after the date on which an eligible entity receives a SMART grant, and annually thereafter until the date on which the SMART grant is expended

evidence.quote: the eligible entity shall submit to the Secretary an implementation report

obligations.summary: Comptroller General shall conduct a review of the SMART grant program and submit a report to the specified Senate and House committees.
obligations.applies_from: Not later than 4 years after the date of enactment of this Act

evidence.quote: the Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct

obligations.summary: Secretary shall submit a report to Congress committees describing each SMART grant recipient, grant amounts, intended uses, effectiveness and lessons learned.
obligations.applies_from: Not later than 2 years after the date on which the initial SMART grants are provided under this section

evidence.quote: the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate

obligations.summary: Secretary shall develop and regularly update SMART grant best practices from data and feedback of recipients and publish them on a publicly available website.

evidence.quote: develop and regularly update best practices based on, among other information, the data, lessons learned, and feedback from eligible entities

obligations.summary: Amended 49 U.S.C. 5505: the Secretary shall make the university transportation centers report available to the public on a Department of Transportation website, replacing the requirement to submit it to Congress; the same change applies to the biennial review under (d)(2)(B)(iii).

evidence.quote: make available to the public on a website of the Department of Transportation

obligations.summary: Amended 49 U.S.C. 5505(d)(2): the review of university transportation centers changes from annual to biennial; the operative review wording is not restated in the amending text.

evidence.quote: by striking annually'' and inserting biennially''

obligations.summary: A regional university transportation center receiving a grant must carry out research focusing on one or more of the matters in 49 U.S.C. 6503(c)(1)(A) through (G).
obligations.conditional_on: Receipt of a grant under 49 U.S.C. 5505(c)(3)

evidence.quote: shall carry out research focusing on 1 or more of the matters described in subparagraphs (A) through (G) of section 6503(c)(1)

enforcement.note: The excerpted sections (40210, 40433, 40531-40535, 11401, 13005, 25005, 25017) set up grant programs, studies and reports and contain no fines, penalties, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking. Section 11401(5)(D)(ii) refers to a contractual remedy and opportunity to cure in an agreement the Secretary considers when selecting grantees, which is not an enforcement sanction and is not coded here.
